title: Interactive Authentication and Brute-Force Defense Policy
scope: All enterprise Linux workstations, production servers, and virtualized workloads.
purpose: To protect enterprise infrastructure from brute-force authentication attacks, credential stuffing, and unauthorized interactive access attempts.
statement: All interactive system logons across enterprise infrastructure must enforce automatic account lockout after a maximum of 5 consecutive failed authentication attempts. Locked accounts must remain inaccessible for at least 15 minutes or until an administrative unlock occurs.
description: Enforces mandatory PAM faillock threshold of 5 attempts and minimum 900-second lockout on all interactive endpoints.
required_evidence_desc: Automated PAM configuration inspection (/etc/security/faillock.conf) and active canary lockout behavioral test evidence.

title: Administrative Least Privilege and Superuser Separation Policy
scope: All enterprise server operating systems, production databases, and container hosts.
purpose: To prevent unauthorized administrative action, reduce blast radius of credential compromise, and enforce strict accountability for privileged operations.
statement: Direct root or superuser logins are prohibited. Administrative operations must be conducted via individualized accounts utilizing audited elevation mechanisms (e.g. sudo). Database superuser privileges must be restricted strictly to automated DBA operational accounts.
description: Prohibits root SSH logins and mandates individualized superuser accounts on Linux and PostgreSQL.
required_evidence_desc: sshd_config PermitRootLogin inspection and PostgreSQL pg_roles superuser audit evidence.

title: Kernel Activity and Security Audit Logging Policy
scope: All production Linux virtual machines and mission-critical application hosts.
purpose: To maintain an immutable, tamper-evident audit record of security-relevant events for compliance, incident investigation, and non-repudiation.
statement: All servers hosting enterprise workloads must execute a persistent, tamper-evident audit logging subsystem. All privilege elevation attempts, authentication successes/failures, and sensitive file modifications must generate immediate audit records.
description: Mandates auditd active service status and syscall audit rules for privilege elevation and authentication.
required_evidence_desc: Systemctl auditd status verification and active auditctl syscall rule enumeration.

title: Database Transmission Encryption and Network Access Policy
scope: All production relational database management systems and analytical warehouses.
purpose: To guarantee transmission confidentiality and protect data in transit against eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.
statement: All connections to production database management systems must be cryptographically protected using TLS 1.2 or higher. Plaintext unencrypted connections must be actively rejected by the database daemon.
description: Enforces mandatory TLS encryption on database listeners and rejection of unencrypted handshakes.
required_evidence_desc: PostgreSQL ssl=on configuration query and behavioral TLS handshake probe rejection evidence.

title: Enterprise Information Security & Governance Charter
scope: Enterprise-wide across all business units, personnel, and technological infrastructure.
purpose: To define the foundational governance structure, risk tolerance, and compliance mandate for the organization.
statement: Management commits to continuous security compliance across ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and NIST SP 800-53 standards. Executive security reviews must occur at least annually.
description: Master governance charter requiring documented policies, continuous assessment, and independent audit readiness.
required_evidence_desc: Annual board review minutes and formal CISO appointment charters.

title: Secure DevSecOps & Production Branch Protection Policy
scope: All enterprise version control repositories and CI/CD pipelines.
purpose: To prevent unauthorized production code deployments and mandate peer review change control.
statement: Direct pushes to production branches (main/master) are strictly prohibited across all source code repositories. Every modification must be initiated via pull request, requiring at least one approving peer review before merging.
description: Enforces mandatory pull request approvals and branch protections across source code repositories.
required_evidence_desc: Repository branch protection configuration and peer-reviewed pull request audit records.

title: Enterprise Acceptable Use Policy
scope: All corporate employees, contractors, third-party workers, and enterprise devices.
purpose: To define clear acceptable use rules, computing standards, and personal responsibility for corporate IT assets and internet connectivity.
statement: Corporate IT assets and communications platforms must be utilized strictly for authorized operational objectives. Unauthorized software installations, credential sharing, and circumventing security mechanisms are strictly prohibited.
description: Establishes acceptable use parameters for workstations, cloud services, messaging channels, and electronic communications.
required_evidence_desc: Signed employee acceptable use acknowledgments and endpoint management software deployment logs.

title: Enterprise IT & Cloud Asset Management Policy
scope: All enterprise hardware, virtual machines, cloud instances, and storage volumes.
purpose: To establish and maintain an authoritative, up-to-date inventory of all technology components and assigned organizational owners.
statement: Every physical server, cloud instance, database, and endpoint must be tracked in an automated Configuration Management Database (CMDB) with assigned system custodians and data classifications.
description: Mandates automated asset discovery, continuous inventory reconciliation, and unauthorized asset isolation.
required_evidence_desc: Automated CMDB synchronization records and cloud infrastructure inventory snapshots.

title: Information Classification and Data Handling Policy
scope: All electronic and physical data processed, transmitted, or stored across the enterprise.
purpose: To classify data according to sensitivity and mandate appropriate technical and operational protective controls.
statement: All enterprise data must be classified into Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted tiers. Restricted data requires mandatory encryption at rest and in transit and strict role-gated access control.
description: Defines four-tier classification taxonomy and handling requirements for customer, business, and operational data.
required_evidence_desc: Data classification register and DLP rule configuration exports.

title: Cryptographic Protection and Key Management Policy
scope: All cryptographic mechanisms, key stores, certificates, and encryption configurations.
purpose: To ensure strong, modern cryptographic algorithms are enforced and cryptographic keys are securely generated, stored, rotated, and retired.
statement: All sensitive data at rest must be encrypted using AES-256 or ChaCha20. Transmission encryption must enforce TLS 1.2 or higher with forward secrecy. Cryptographic keys must be managed in dedicated HSMs or cloud KMS with annual rotation.
description: Governs cipher suite baselines, automated certificate lifecycle management, and HSM key protection.
required_evidence_desc: KMS key rotation audit logs and TLS daemon cipher configuration audits.

title: Vulnerability Identification and Patch Management Policy
scope: All production operating systems, network appliances, containers, and application packages.
purpose: To systematically detect, prioritize, and remediate software and configuration vulnerabilities to prevent exploitation.
statement: Weekly automated vulnerability scans must cover all addressable production IP ranges and container registries. Critical vulnerabilities must be remediated within 7 calendar days; High vulnerabilities within 30 days.
description: Mandates automated scanning cadences, severity-based SLA remediation windows, and patch deployment verification.
required_evidence_desc: Automated scanner coverage reports and patch management deployment audit trails.

title: Security Incident Response and Notification Policy
scope: All security events, system anomalies, and suspected breaches across enterprise infrastructure.
purpose: To ensure rapid, coordinated containment, eradication, recovery, and defensible evidence preservation during security incidents.
statement: Suspected security breaches must be declared and escalated to the Incident Response Team within 1 hour of verification. Containment actions must prioritize evidence preservation in accordance with legal and regulatory mandates.
description: Defines incident classification matrix, triage procedures, containment playbooks, and regulatory notification obligations.
required_evidence_desc: Incident management ticketing logs, tabletop simulation minutes, and post-mortem review archives.

title: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy
scope: All mission-critical business systems, cloud regions, and core communications channels.
purpose: To guarantee operational resilience and ensure critical business systems can recover within defined RTO and RPO objectives.
statement: Tier-1 business applications must maintain an RTO of under 4 hours and an RPO of under 1 hour. Multi-region redundancy and annual failover testing are mandatory.
description: Establishes business continuity planning, disaster recovery failover architectures, and operational resilience testing.
required_evidence_desc: Annual DR failover test reports and executive business impact analysis (BIA) documentation.

title: Data Backup, Retention, and Restoration Policy
scope: All production database clusters, object storage buckets, and file systems.
purpose: To protect enterprise data against accidental deletion, ransomware extortion, and system corruption through verified backups.
statement: All production datastores must execute automated daily incremental snapshots and weekly full backups with 30-day immutability. Quarterly restoration rehearsals must be conducted and documented.
description: Mandates write-once-read-many (WORM) backup storage, offsite replication, and routine recovery rehearsals.
required_evidence_desc: Automated backup execution metrics and quarterly restore verification tickets.

title: Enterprise System and Infrastructure Change Management Policy
scope: All production networks, hosts, databases, and application runtime environments.
purpose: To ensure changes to production environments are reviewed, risk-assessed, tested, and tracked to prevent outages.
statement: Direct unapproved modifications to production systems are strictly forbidden. All modifications require a logged change request with peer review, test evidence, and an automated rollback plan.
description: Standardizes change classification, CAB approval gating, emergency change procedures, and audit record keeping.
required_evidence_desc: Approved change management tickets and CI/CD automated deployment audit records.

title: Secure Baseline Configuration and Hardening Policy
scope: All operating systems, container base images, and cloud virtual appliances.
purpose: To establish consistent security hardening baselines across all deployed assets and minimize attack surfaces.
statement: All Linux hosts and database servers must comply with Center for Internet Security (CIS) Level 1 benchmarks. Non-essential services, default credentials, and insecure legacy protocols must be disabled prior to production deployment.
description: Mandates standardized golden images, configuration management via code (Ansible/Terraform), and automated drift detection.
required_evidence_desc: Automated CIS compliance scanning telemetry and Infrastructure-as-Code state audits.

title: Network Security and Perimeter Defense Policy
scope: All corporate perimeters, cloud virtual networks (VPCs), subnets, and firewalls.
purpose: To control traffic between security domains, protect boundaries, and isolate critical data through micro-segmentation.
statement: All ingress and egress traffic must traverse stateful firewalls configured with explicit allow-lists and default-deny policies. Direct public internet access to production database and management ports is strictly prohibited.
description: Enforces network segmentation, VPN multifactor authentication, and continuous firewall rule reviews.
required_evidence_desc: Cloud Security Group configuration dumps and stateful firewall rule change audit records.

title: Third-Party and Vendor Risk Management Policy
scope: All SaaS providers, infrastructure vendors, external consultants, and technology partners.
purpose: To assess and manage cybersecurity risks introduced through external suppliers and supply-chain partners.
statement: Before onboarding, third parties handling corporate or customer data must undergo security due diligence (SOC 2 or ISO 27001 review). Vendor agreements must include mandatory breach notification clauses within 24 hours.
description: Governs vendor security tiering, contractual security commitments, and annual re-assessment cycles.
required_evidence_desc: Completed vendor risk assessments and annual SOC 2 report review records.

title: Information Security Risk Assessment and Treatment Policy
scope: All business units, digital products, and IT operations.
purpose: To establish a formalized, repeatable methodology for identifying, analyzing, evaluating, and mitigating cybersecurity risks.
statement: Formal risk assessments must be executed annually or upon significant architectural changes. Identified risks exceeding tolerance thresholds must have approved risk treatment plans or formal executive risk acceptance waivers.
description: Standardizes risk scoring matrices, risk appetite boundaries, and treatment tracking registers.
required_evidence_desc: Enterprise risk register and executive risk treatment signoff minutes.

title: Security Awareness and Role-Based Training Policy
scope: All enterprise personnel, contractors, and specialized engineering staff.
purpose: To build a resilient security culture and ensure personnel understand their duties, threat vectors, and safe operating practices.
statement: All newly onboarded personnel must complete security awareness training within 14 days of hire, and annually thereafter. Software engineers and system administrators must complete role-specific secure coding and privilege management training.
description: Defines general employee training requirements, simulated phishing testing, and specialized engineering curriculums.
required_evidence_desc: Learning management system completion records and phishing simulation response statistics.

title: Physical and Environmental Security Policy
scope: All corporate offices, server rooms, data center colocations, and badged facilities.
purpose: To protect infrastructure, communications hardware, and personnel against physical intrusion, theft, and environmental perils.
statement: All facility access must be controlled via electronic badge readers with visitor logs. Server rooms and network closets must enforce dual-factor biometric or keycard access with 90-day CCTV video retention.
description: Enforces physical perimeter barriers, environmental controls (fire suppression, HVAC, UPS), and visitor escort protocols.
required_evidence_desc: Electronic badge reader access logs and facility CCTV inspection audits.

title: Data Retention, Archival, and Media Sanitization Policy
scope: All electronic storage media, database backups, audit records, and decommissioned drives.
purpose: To define compliant data retention schedules and enforce secure cryptographic media sanitization prior to disposal or reuse.
statement: Audit logs must be retained for at least 365 days. Storage media containing sensitive data must be cryptographically wiped or physically degaussed/shredded in compliance with NIST SP 800-88 Rev 1 guidelines.
description: Establishes retention schedules by data type and mandates certificates of destruction for retired hardware.
required_evidence_desc: Automated log retention lifecycle policies and third-party media destruction certificates.
